learning_outcomes.text: Interpret the physical meaning of the general properties of fluids.
Know and apply the conservation equations to fluid flow.
Know the characteristics of the main flows of interest in engineering (pressure flow, open channel flow, external flow).
Know the operating principles and operation of basic instruments for measuring pressure, flow rate, velocity, and viscosity.
Design fluid installations, applying efficiency criteria in the design of the installation.
Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and their application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels and fluid systems.

syllabus_topics: Fluids: definition; compressible and incompressible fluids; viscosity and density.
Fluid flow: definition, types of flow.
Principles of fluid statics: General theorem of statics; Pascal's Principle; Buoyancy.
Flow domain. Lagrangian and Eulerian description.
Flow rate through an elemental surface.
Reynolds Transport Theorem: application to mass, momentum, and energy.
Differential equations of continuity and Navier-Stokes.
General characteristics of Internal Flow. Flow regime. Fully developed flow and entrance length.
Velocity and pressure profile in laminar flow.
Velocity and pressure profile in turbulent flow.
Calculation of the required power for flow.
Measurement of flow rates in open channels.
Models of compressible flow of ideal gases. Adiabatic, Isentropic flow. Nozzles and Diffusers. Isothermal flow.
Resistance to flow of submerged bodies. Characteristic area. Friction drag and form drag.
teaching_methods: Submission of exercises proposed by professors, to be solved by students
Written final test, performed individually in the classroom, containing theoretical and numerical questions
Two seminars for analysis and resolution of practical cases, performed individually in the classroom with the assistance of the two professors of the subject.
Fluid Engineering laboratory practices, performed in groups and consisting of experimental practices.
Attendance at master class sessions where concepts and contents of the different topics will be systematically developed.
Performing three laboratory practices and one CFD simulation in groups.
assessment_rules: The general evaluation model is continuous assessment. No single evaluation activity can individually exceed 60% of the global grade. The sum of non-re-evaluable activities cannot exceed 40% of the global grade. For the written exam (55% weight), a minimum grade of 5 is required, and it is re-evaluable; the exam has a theoretical part (40% of exam grade) and a problem part (60%), both requiring a minimum of 4 to be averaged. Attendance to laboratory practices is mandatory, and absence will result in failing the subject in both calls. The final course grade must be 5 or higher, calculated as the weighted average of all activities.
